<!--
Keep this issue as small as the problem allows.

Lead with the conclusion: what is wrong or worth changing, and what follows from it.

Delete any section that does not add useful information. Add a more specific section when the
issue calls for it, such as Reproduction, Environment, Measurements, or Current behaviour.

If another concern can be implemented and closed independently, split it into a separate issue.
-->

## Summary

<!--
What is wrong, missing, or worth changing? Include the consequence when it is not obvious.

For a small issue, this may be most of the issue.
-->

## Evidence

<!-- Optional.
Only include what supports the claim: reproduction, measurements, logs, examples, or relevant code.
Delete this section when the problem is already clear.
-->

## Proposed change

<!-- Optional.
Describe the intended change or the next investigation.
Do not turn this into a complete implementation plan unless those details are necessary to define
the issue.
-->

## Verification

<!-- Optional.
What test, observation, or benchmark would show that this is resolved?
One sentence is enough when the answer is obvious.
-->

## Scope

<!-- Optional.
Use this only when the work could easily expand. State what belongs in this issue and what should be
handled separately.
-->
